why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Check 1's PASS asks that the --tsv output "parses as a JSON array that is deep-equal to" the CSV command's array. Its FAIL covers an error, output that is not a JSON array, or a different array. The words "prints the same JSON array" require exactly that. Check 2's PASS asks that README.md "mentions the --tsv flag and says what it does". "Documents" means more than just naming the flag, and no exact wording is required, so this is not stricter than the words. The stricter tests are under the Advisory heading and are not PASS/FAIL conditions: npm test, whether a test covers --tsv, unchanged plain CSV behaviour, and byte-for-byte stdout with exit status 0. No branch rule, file-scope rule, mutation test or exact-wording rule appears in any PASS or FAIL condition.
